summary: The offline harness only exercised the happy path, so the runner, scheduler, orchestrator and audit safety rules were never driven end to end by a failing game. Scenario accounts can now list faults: a snapshot read that fails, a call that raises after taking effect, an ambiguous (non-boolean) response, the player spending between snapshots, and a snapshot labelled with another account. Faults trigger on counted invocations (per day or per run) or with a probability drawn from a generator seeded by the scenario seed and alias, so reports stay byte-identical for the same seed and the game's own random amounts are untouched.  Two shipped scenarios and regression tests assert the outcomes: an unobserved effect is unknown, never verified; a non-idempotent retry is refused after an uncertain outcome; uncertain spend is journaled as <kind>_uncertain and charged by spent_in_period and the audit; a foreign snapshot ends that account with no calls while others run; a contradicted collection stops the account. The baseline scenarios carry no faults and their reports are unchanged (hash-compared before/after). Implemented by the test specialist subagent in an isolated worktree, independently reviewed by the verifier subagent (APPROVE-WITH-NITS; strict fault validation added in 717b7fe), and re-validated by the parent.
